title: Started wonderfully, now less happy after nearly 2 years.
text:
Started wonderfully, now less happy after nearly 2 years.. Update(June 2012): hmm, not happy with it, the non stick became sticky. The coating obviously didn't last long. Decided it would be a waste of time to test the warranty as I don't want the same wok with the same problem. So I now have a ceramic coated wok.

Original review:
Almost a five star. The finish of the wok is truely high class, compared with a lot of the 'non'stick' varieties out there. We have been looking for a decent non-stick wok for almost a year: hunting from william sonoma, china town, crate and barrel and web sites. why this amount of passion? we love cooking with a wok, but our recent wok, a non-stick, and despite the seasoning - it just did not work. With a lot of claims on the non-stick material peeling off and the danger it poses to our health. We finally buckled as the cleaning and the sticking on the non-stick wok was just taking the enjoyment out of cooking. I think you have to bash this wok around before feeling happens. We think the non stick finish is a lot better than the All Clad brand, which we noticed had started to peel a few applications.

After a couple of heavy duty sessions with our wok, including a dinner party of 6, we love it. the only grip is that we wish it could be 2 inches deeper, as per traditional wok. hence you can toss and stir fry like in a traditional wok, but we are living with it as it as the food is not sticking/burning and the cleaning is a dream. Note that there is a 25 years warranty on this product so scan a copy of this invoice, note down the address that is attached to the wok and save it in your email box! If it serves me for 25 years, I think I certainly got my return on the cost! The 12 inch is not that wide, and I would highly recommend for a family of two to a party up to 8.

product_metadata.title: Joyce Chen 22-0030, Pro Chef Peking Pan with Excalibur Non-stick coating, 12-Inch
features: Versatile carbon steel pan sears satisfying stir fry, but also great for veggies and eggs
Premium Excalibur nonstick coating resists scratching—even with metal utensils
2.0mm professional carbon steel gauge is lighter and stronger than cast iron; heats evenly with no hot spots
Flat bottom and sloped sides are ideal for searing and sautéing
Resin handle stays cool and remains oven safe up to 350 degrees
Without removable handle, pan lets food simmer up to 500 degrees
description: Cook like a pro with this versatile stir-fry pan. A smaller, shallower version of the flat-bottom carbon steel wok, this pan can be used for so many dishes beyond stir-fry—from sauteed veggies to scrambled eggs. Made from carbon steel, it’s lighter and smoother than cast iron, yet just as hardy, with a nonstick coating tough even to withstand the scrapes and rakes of metal utensils. When you pop off the removable resin handle, this pan can also go from stovetop to oven to keep dishes simmering up to 500 degrees.
